# v0.10.7 - Two Ways An Upload Could Fail

## What's Changed in v0.10.7

A fixes-only release (soft maintenance mode): two ways an upload could fail, both found by measuring a real Seafile CE 13.0 container. Each fix has tests that fail without it.

### Fixed
- **A chunked upload that took longer than an hour failed.** An upload link is checked on every chunk and expires an hour after it was issued (`web_token_expire_time`, default 3600 s), and the client used the one link it got for the first chunk until the last. Measured on a CE 13.0 container with the lifetime set to 60 s: a chunk sent on an expired link is not read and gets no answer (a timeout or an aborted connection; only a very small body gets a `403`), and the upload failed. A 50 GiB payload or LFS upload slower than about 14 MiB/s therefore died at the hour. The client now asks for a fresh link before it sends a chunk on one older than 45 minutes, and after a chunk failed by timeout, reset or `403` (the partial is kept by path, not by token, so the upload continues), up to eight times per upload. The same upload then finished with the right SHA-256.
- **An upload was refused with `400 Bad request.` about once in 512 to 4096 times, for any content.** The server's upload parser (`upload-file.c`) consumes the closing `--boundary--` line without its trailing CRLF, so when the very last network read of the body is only that 2-byte CRLF it reads it as a blank header line and answers `400`. Behind the usual nginx the reads are 4096 bytes, so a body of 4096 * k + 2 bytes failed every time (measured on CE 13.0: of 4,200 consecutive body lengths only those failed; the same file with a different name length uploaded fine). A retry has the same length and fails again, so a push, an LFS transfer or a payload upload could stop on one file. The multipart boundary is now lengthened until the body is not 2 past a multiple of 512, and small uploads from memory use the same framing. A reproduction and the report for the Seafile project are in the specs repository (`tools/repro_upload_400.py`).

### Upgrading

Nothing about what is stored changes and no setting is renamed. See "Upgrading to v0.10.7" in `UPGRADING.md`.

The full list is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
